decisions.rationale: Temperature-to-thermal-motion relation is a foundational heat concept with no canonical collision.

This tests the same temperature/thermal-motion proposition as C001 by reversing the direction to cooling. It does not add a distinct reasoning boundary and is prohibited filler under the 600Q contract.
Mass conservation across a closed-system state change is distinct from the temperature-motion items.
Melting point as the solid/liquid boundary is a distinct state-change definition.
Boiling point as the liquid/gas boundary is a separate concept from melting point and directly relevant to volatile liquids.
Particle thermal motion versus interparticle force provides an explanatory model rather than another state-name recall.
Physical-change classification distinguishes state change from chemical change and has independent educational value.
Chemical decomposition terminology is distinct from physical-change and state-boundary items.
Internal-energy terminology supports later work/heat reasoning and is not represented in the canonical baseline.
Kelvin as the SI unit of absolute temperature is a precise standalone foundation item.
Natural heat-flow direction is distinct from the canonical combustion cooling question, which tests removal of the heat leg of combustion.
Heat lost equals heat gained in an isolated pair is a separate conservation relation from heat-flow direction.
Heat-capacity comparison tests whole-object thermal response and is materially distinct from specific heat.
Specific-heat comparison explicitly uses the mass-normalized Q=mcΔT relation, creating a distinct decision boundary from C013.
Latent heat is an independent state-change heat concept absent from the canonical baseline.
Thermal expansion tests dimensional response to heating rather than temperature or heat-transfer terminology.
Adiabatic rapid-compression heating is a useful hazardous-material ignition mechanism and a distinct work-to-internal-energy application.
Mechanical-work dissipation into heat is a separate energy-conversion application from gas compression.
Density as a characteristic property supports substance identification and complements, rather than duplicates, substance-specific B4 density values.
Atomic structure is foundational chemistry knowledge with no canonical or Wave 1 semantic collision.

collision_review.note: C002 is rejected as a semantic mirror of C001. The remaining 19 candidates add distinct definitions, conservation relations, thermal-property comparisons, energy-conversion applications or matter-structure knowledge.
